reasoning_summary: Part 1 (lines 0011-0018) is essentially sound: in a 2-connected plane graph every face boundary is a cycle (line 0012 states this correct standard fact, if tersely justified), and the alternation/parity argument closing the cycle at line 0017 is valid. Part 2 fails. The ear-decomposition induction (lines 0022-0039) needs, for an ear P added to a bipartite subgraph H, that the parity of P is forced by the colors of its endpoints. Line 0031 supplies this by asserting that 'the boundary of the new face created by adding P must be an even cycle' -- i.e. it applies the hypothesis (every face of G has even boundary) to a face of the intermediate subgraph H'. Faces of H' are not faces of G: a face of H' is generally a union of many faces of G together with the edges of G interior to it, and its bounding closed walk is not among the face boundaries whose parity is hypothesized. So the appeal at line 0031 is unjustified. (The correct argument -- that the boundary of such a region is a symmetric difference of face boundaries of G in the cycle space, hence even -- is exactly the content that must be proved and is nowhere supplied; the standard proof instead uses the fact that the face boundaries generate the cycle space.) The subsequent text (lines 0032-0037) does not repair this: it only restates that the two parities 'must match appropriately' and concludes 'the coloring can be extended consistently' by assertion rather than deriving that an ear joining two same-colored vertices has even length. A secondary defect appears already at line 0028, where the ear's endpoints are taken to be colored 'red and blue', silently excluding the case of two like-colored endpoints, which is precisely the case the induction must handle.
